newsitem.title: USA: Gorbachev criticizes U.S. on military spending.
newsitem.headline: Gorbachev criticizes U.S. on military spending.

text.p: Former Soviet President Mikhail Gorbachev sharply criticised the U.S. Congress on Wednesday for authorising higher military spending than the Clinton administration had asked for.

Gorbachev said the U.S. military budget as well as plans for the eastward expansion of NATO had caused many Russians to doubt the desirability of implementing arms control treaties. He warned this could spark a reaction that would benefit people who had resisted ending the Cold War.

Gorbachev, who played a large part in defusing the Cold War, gave the warning during a speech kicking off the second annual "State of the World Forum," a gathering of politicians, business executives, scientists and religious figures from around the world.

Gorbachev said the "powerful momentum" of arms reduction that started in the mid-1980s was weakening and militarism was regaining ground. Military spending had been substantially reduced only in Russia and countries of the Commonwealth of Independent States (CIS), he said.

He noted that the U.S. Congress had authorised more military spending for the new fiscal year than the Pentagon had asked for, saying this was "a unique event in probably the history of the United States."
The Republican-dominated Congress last month sent President Bill Clinton a $265.6 billion defence bill calling for $11 billion more spending than he wanted.

"The remaining superpower, which is not being threatened by anyone, wants to protect its security and its national interest by the use of weapons, by the use of force. Is that how we should understand this decision?" Gorbachev asked the large crowd at the opening dinner. "What kind of signal does the United States send to other countries?"

"And in Russia, given this fact and also the plans for the expansion of NATO to the East, many people in Russian society are beginning to doubt the desirability of implementing the agreements and treaties on arms control and this is the first symptom of reaction," he said through an interpreter.

"I believe this can become a mutually reinforcing process that will only help those who were against arms control and disarmament in the first place and those who resisted ending the Cold War," Gorbachev added.

"When we see military spending at a very high level compared to military spending in Russia and when there's even a possibility that arms spending will begin to rise once again, you will see a response, you will see a very acute reaction and this will complicate the situation not only in Russia but elsewhere," Gorbachev said.
"This will provide ammunition to those who would like to set us back to the old times," he said, referring to the Cold War.
